title: Pairs
statement: Implement `solve(left, right)`. Return the cartesian product as a list of `[a, b]` pairs. `a` changes in the outer loop, so all pairs for the first left item come before the next left item. Either side empty returns an empty list.
constraints: left and right are lists of strings
hints: For each a in left, for each b in right, emit [a, b].
Do not emit [b, a] unless the inputs happen to make that equal.
Empty on either side short-circuits to no pairs.
editorial: Nested loops are the product. The outer choice fixes the order tests will check. Swapping the loops is a different sequence, not a sorting detail, because the problem asks for outer-left order.
reference_solution:
def solve(left, right):
    return [[a, b] for a in left for b in right]
